chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Suleiman ibn Sama'ah from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to them, and the Prophet was enshrouded, and in the house were Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them).
He said: Peace be upon you, O People of the House of Mercy! Every soul shall taste death.
And only will you be given in full your reward on the Day of Resurrection; so whoever is removed away from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise he indeed has succeeded.
And what is the life of the world except the enjoyment of deception.
Indeed, in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a consolation from every calamity, and a successor to every dying one, and a attainment for what is lost.
So in Allah rely, and to Him hope, for indeed the one who is afflicted is the one who is deprived of the reward.
This is my last stepping of the world.
They said: We heard the voice but did not see the person.

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِ الرَّحْمَةِ: People of the House of Mercy

ai.seo_question: What happened when the Prophet Muhammad passed away according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* records the visit of Jibraeel to the Ahl al-Bayt immediately after the Prophet's passing, offering divine consolation (*azā'*) by affirming that every deceased has a successor in Allah. It highlights the Shia theological perspective that true loss is missing the reward (*thawāb*), while the physical absence of the angel underscores the spiritual nature of this divine communication. The narration serves as a foundational text for the etiquette of condolences, linking the Prophet's death to the broader Islamic promise of resurrection and ultimate success.
